# Immutable ledger entry row

> One immutable database row representing a single line of a double-entry journal, with an account, a signed amount in cents, and a journal ID that groups related lines.

_Part of [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md)_

A [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) is the smallest unit in the ledger: one line saying "account X gained or lost Y cents." When [LedgerService posts a journal](recording-money-in-ledger.md), it creates one entry per account involved—buyer, seller, platform—all tagged with the same `journalId` so they stay together. The rows never change after creation (`updatedAt` and `deletedAt` are both disabled in the schema), so once the ledger says something happened, it stays true. The `amount` field uses positive for credits (money in) and negative for debits (money out). A `journalId` groups all the lines of a balanced posting together; the database rejects any journal whose lines don't sum to exactly zero, enforcing double-entry bookkeeping. Each entry also stores `kind` (like `SALE`, `SETTLEMENT`, `PAYOUT`) and an optional `paymentId` link back to the [Payment](payment-records.md) that triggered it.

**Look at:** [`LedgerEntry` in ledger-entry.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/ledger-entry.model.ts#L79)

## Pieces

- [Journal type enum (SALE, SETTLEMENT, PAYOUT, etc.)](recording-money-in-ledger.md): Enum of the kinds of journals: SALE (customer payment), SETTLEMENT (split to shops), PAYOUT (weekly payout), `PAYOUT_REVERSAL` (failed payout), REFUND (card refund), ADJUSTMENT, `AD_CHARGE`.
- [Signed BIGINT amount in cents: positive = credit, negative = debit](ledger-amount-convention.md): The `amount` field is a signed integer; positive means money came in (credit), negative means money went out (debit). Always stored in cents, never dollars.
- [Immutable rows: once written, never updated or deleted](ledger-immutability.md): The ORM model disables `updatedAt` and `deletedAt` so entries never change. Once a line is posted, it is permanent.
- journalId field groups lines of one balanced posting: All entries created together have the same `journalId`. The database enforces that all lines of a journal sum to zero.

Read by {{shop-balance-read-model\|[`BalanceProjector`](shop-balance-read-model.md)}} to project account balances; written by {{recording-money-in-ledger\|[`LedgerService`](recording-money-in-ledger.md)}} as part of journal posting. |

## Watch out

- The `@Scopes` decorator and `PaymentWithAllFilters` interface in the source code appear to be copy-pasted from the Payment model and do not actually apply to [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) queries.
- Signed amounts are the opposite of common accounting language: positive is credit (money in), negative is debit (money out)—remember the sign, not the label.
- A `journalId` is just a UUID; if you lose track of which entries belong together, you have orphaned lines. Always group by `journalId` when reasoning about a posting.
- Once created, entries are forever. There is no update, no soft delete, no 'I changed my mind.' Immutability is enforced by the ORM, so never try to fix a posted line—post a reversing entry instead.
